text:
elaine: Quick question — for private/VPC customers, should we lean on a local read-only control-plane cache inside the tenant VPC (lightweight daemonset + local kv cache) to answer cert/tenant-metadata lookups, or require customers to use a PrivateLink/Private Endpoint to the control plane?

rob: what are the hard requirements here? latency SLA, consistency, and audit footprint?

simon: TL;DR: cache wins for p95 latency and egress reduction. Big caveat: revocations/rollbacks. caches with TTLs + invalidation channels are needed.

jules: Agree with simon. Also consider operational surface — we add lifecycle for the daemonset in customer spaces. Who owns upgrades?

elaine: Good point. Main constraints I heard: 1) no customer traffic crossing public internet, 2) revocation (<30s ideal for certain certs), 3) central audit/logs must be preserved. PrivateLink satisfies (1) and (3) but struggles with (latency) and cost.

rob: Could we do hybrid: local cache for reads (fast), but push invalidation via an outbound-only websocket or pubsub tunnel to cache agents? That keeps egress minimal (customer -> CP) and avoids inbound peering.

simon: Outbound-only invalidation is promising. Example flow: cache agent subscribes to CP invalidation topic over TLS to our relay, CP publishes revocation IDs. Agent invalidates TTL entries. Best-effort but we can add sequence numbers to avoid race.

jules: Ops questions: how do we prove audit provenance? If agent serves a cert lookup, we need the request to be logged centrally with tenant identity. Two choices: 1) agent forwards a log event to CP over the same outbound channel; 2) agent attaches a signed assertion we ingest later. Option 1 keeps real-time audit but increases egress.

elaine: On rotation: short-lived signed assertions from CP (e.g., 1m validity) + agent caches them for that TTL. Rotation requires push invalidation. If invalidation channel fails, agent should fallback to calling PrivateLink (if configured) or degrade to 403.

rob: Fallback policy sketch (pseudocode):
```
if cache.hit() and not expired:
  return cached
else if invalidation_channel.ok:
  pull latest and update cache
else if private_endpoint.available:
  call private_endpoint
else:
  return 403
```

jules: We need a plan for upgrades: helm-managed daemonset with sidecar that auto-updates minor versions but requires explicit opt-in for major changes. That keeps support burden bounded.

simon: Security: HSM/KMS keys must stay in customer's control for signing? If we ask agent to sign assertions locally, keys live in customer env — good for compliance but painful for us. Alternatively, agent forwards CSR to CP over PrivateLink and CP signs. Tradeoff: more egress vs control.

elaine: Proposed decision (narrow): implement outbound-only invalidation + read-only cache agent as opt-in for tenants. Default remains PrivateLink. For tenants that opt into local cache we require: short TTLs, invalidation channel enabled, signed audit events forwarded.

rob: +1 for opt-in. Suggest we prototype with 3 customers first and measure staleness and egress metrics.

jules: Will draft rollout checklist: helm chart, invalidation topic, metrics (staleness, cache-hit, egress bytes), and runbook for failed invalidation.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket RED-NTW-412 for prototype + added owners @elaine @simon @jules :spiral_notepad: 

elaine: Thanks — I'll add a short RFC follow-up that pins the fallback policy and the audit requirements. Keep comments here for anything I missed.
